tasks.spec:
You are fixing ONE identity bug in ONE Python file. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES:
  1. scripts/guest_candidate_feed.py   (edit it)
  2. fix-summary.md                    (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check.

## The bug

That file already has a helper that has been there all along:

    def alias_for(name_key: str) -> str:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(name_key.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:10]
        return f"cand-{digest}"

That is the person's IDENTITY. It is derived from their normalised name, so the same person is the same alias on Tuesday as on Monday, whatever order the inbox happens to arrive in. Downstream, server/pipeline/guest_outreach_draft.py copies it straight into `candidate_key` in every receipt and in the draft ledger — and that ledger is what the owner's first-draft gate counts when it holds the first three drafts for review.

The most recent change introduced a SECOND, positional alias scheme alongside it:

    contact_alias = f"cand-{chr(ord('a') + position)}" if position < 26 else f"cand-{position + 1}"

So the same person is `cand-a` today and `cand-b` tomorrow if one record is added above them, and two different people are both `cand-a` on different days. Worse, the file is now inconsistent with itself: drop-report entries use the stable alias_for() alias while selected candidates go out under the positional one, so one report describes the same person two different ways.

## The fix

Delete the positional scheme. Use `alias_for(key)` — where `key` is the already-computed `normalized_name(candidate['name'])` — as the ONE alias, everywhere:

  * in the `people` list handed to contact_index.build(), as the "alias" field,
  * as the argument to contact_index.resolve(...),
  * in the evidence_ref of the second-order observations built from the intake note and the ledger last_touch,
  * in every drop() entry,
  * and in the "alias" of each selected candidate in the output.

Change nothing else. Every other behaviour landed yesterday and is verified: cheap filters run before any contact lookup, only survivors are sent to the adapters, the intake note and an older ledger touch arrive as grounded second-order observations, only a NO_CONTACT_FOUND verdict is selected, drop reasons name the verdict and the unread channels, the report carries contact_coverage, and no name, address or note text appears in the report. Do not restructure, do not rename anything else, do not 'improve' neighbouring code. This is a small, surgical diff.

## Run the exact check until it prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u15_contact_gate_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

Right now it fails with F8_alias_not_stable, F8_emitted_alias_wrong and F8_alias_moved_with_position, plus F3 and F4 failures that are downstream of the same bug — the check hands the contact index evidence filed under the person's stable alias, and a feeder asking about 'cand-a' never finds it. Fixing the alias fixes all five. Read the failure text; it names the expected value.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of the check command. Under 400 words.
tasks.verified: Re-runs the full contact-gate check, which now pins identity as well as safety: the alias the feeder uses to ask about a person, the alias in the drop report and the alias on the selected candidate must all equal the name-derived alias_for() value, and must not change when that person arrives at a different position in the inbox. The holding and clearing scenarios still all execute, so the fix cannot be bought by weakening the gate.
